document_title: Process Characterization Report — Small-Virus Retentive Filtration (Step 9)
schema_note: Blocks validate against nlp_reports app/models; parameter_type, document_type, QualityAttribute criticality fields, StudyDesign and DesignSpace are local extensions (see schema_extensions_used).
schema_extensions_used: ProvenAcceptableRange (new model) — per-CQA x parameter PAR (at-set-point / NOR-propagated); both viral CQAs use a back-calculated step floor
RhetoricalSpan (new model) — argument-structure roles over the report prose
out_of_schema_notes: Virus filtration sets no CQA; the QualityAttribute entities are the viral-clearance CQAs it controls/clears (cumulative, cross-step).
Per-step MVM/XMuLV log-reductions are modular contributions with no released spec; reported via studies/report_sections.

Two-factor design: the 2^2 screen is FULL, not fractional, so no effect is aliased and the usual near-saturation caution does not apply; the limitation that does apply is curvature, which is why the RSM remains the predictive model and the basis of the design space.

XMuLV log-reduction and step yield produced no significant term and both fits have negative predicted R²; they are robustness evidence and are explicitly not used predictively, so no DesignSpace or model claim is recorded for them.
Process-capability (Cpk) values have no dedicated field; reported as report_sections statements.
proven_acceptable_ranges mirror @tbl-par (doe_report.par_table), one record per rendered row; rhetorical_spans are verbatim report prose.

PCR-009 carries one registered weak claim (WC-009-01, unbounded_generalization) at the close of the capability section. It is deliberately NOT covered by an assertion or a rhetorical span; the grounded statements that bound it (Stage-2 confirmation, the scale-down bound, the load limit) are annotated instead.

process_steps.description: Small-virus retentive (size-exclusion) filtration: the dedicated virus-removal step. Retains virus larger than the membrane rating while the antibody monomer transmits. Sets no product-quality CQA; it is the principal contributor to the cumulative MVM (parvovirus) log-reduction and a major contributor to the enveloped-virus (XMuLV) log-reduction, credited as orthogonal/modular clearance under ICH Q5A(R2).

source_references.quote: Small-virus retentive filtration is Step 9 of the A-Mab drug-substance process and the last step at which virus is removed.
a qualified small-scale spiking model of the commercial filtration operation, and the qualification followed the scale-down model procedure (SOP-1001)

parameters.rationale_for_criticality: Either quality-linked through a demonstrated effect on MVM clearance (the volumetric-load limit), or held inside the range in which the clearance claim was demonstrated even though no effect was resolved; in both cases the risk of leaving the characterized range is low — the load is fixed before the batch by the pool volume and the installed membrane area and verified against the batch record, and the pressure is held by the controller against its set-point.

design_spaces.definition: The whole characterized rectangle in volumetric load and filtration pressure: everywhere inside the characterized ranges the response-surface model keeps the MVM log-reduction above the back-calculated step requirement, and measured XMuLV clearance stayed above its requirement at every executed run. The principal plane of the region is the load axis, because load is the only parameter with a resolved effect; the region is nonetheless expressed over both parameters, because the demonstration that clearance is insensitive to pressure holds only across the pressure range that was studied. The worst case is the highest load at the pressure at which the fitted surface is lowest.

statements.statement_text: Both process parameters (volumetric load and filtration pressure) are well-controlled CPPs; the step carries no CPP and no key process parameter.

source_references.quote: Both parameters are classified as well-controlled critical process parameters (WC-CPP). There is no critical process parameter and no key process parameter at this step.

statements.statement_text: MVM (parvovirus) clearance falls as the volumetric load rises, and that is the only parameter effect the study resolved.

source_references.quote: Clearance of minute virus of mice (MVM) falls as the volumetric load rises, and that is the only parameter effect the study resolved.

statements.statement_text: XMuLV clearance and step yield are robustness findings: no model term reached significance and neither fit is used predictively.

source_references.quote: Their response-surface models are reported as robustness evidence and are not used predictively.

statements.statement_text: Only the MVM (parvovirus) response-surface model is adequate for prediction, and it is the predictive model on which the design space rests.

source_references.quote: The parvovirus model is adequate and is used predictively

statements.statement_text: With two factors the screening design is a full factorial, so no effect is aliased and the usual near-saturation caution does not apply; the limitation that does apply is curvature, which is why the response-surface model stays predictive.

source_references.quote: so no effect is aliased with another and both main effects and the interaction are estimated independently

statements.statement_text: The load effect is close to linear across the characterized range: the quadratic term in load does not reach significance and the decline does not accelerate towards the upper edge.

source_references.quote: so the decline is close to linear over the range studied and does not accelerate towards the upper edge

statements.statement_text: The MVM model passes its lack-of-fit test without a comfortable margin, which is why every assurance statement is made from the NOR-propagated predictive interval and not from a point prediction.

source_references.quote: its lack-of-fit test passes without a comfortable margin, which is why the assurance statements are made from the NOR-propagated predictive interval and not from point predictions

statements.statement_text: The adverse load trend is bounded: the worst case the design space must satisfy is the highest load at the pressure where the fitted surface is lowest, and it still meets the back-calculated step requirement.

source_references.quote: The worst case the region must satisfy is the highest load combined with the pressure at which the fitted surface is lowest.

statements.statement_text: The reported capability figures are properties of the whole process and not of this step: parvovirus clearance is delivered jointly with anion exchange (PCR-008).

source_references.quote: The capability figures are properties of the process and not of this step.

statements.statement_text: The cumulative parvovirus clearance attribute carries the lowest process-capability index of any A-Mab drug-substance attribute.

source_references.quote: The parvovirus figure is the lowest capability of any A-Mab drug-substance attribute

assertions.assertion_text: Volumetric load has a demonstrated effect on MVM clearance — the only effect resolved at this step — so it is quality-linked and classified WC-CPP.

source_references.quote: Filtration volume (load) is a WC-CPP. It is the only parameter with a demonstrated effect on a critical quality attribute, and the effect is adverse in direction

assertions.assertion_text: No term involving filtration pressure was significant for either clearance response or for step yield; it is classified WC-CPP on bounding logic, because ICH Q5A(R2) ties the clearance claim to the conditions under which it was demonstrated.

source_references.quote: Filtration pressure is a WC-CPP. No term involving pressure was significant for either clearance response or for step yield, in either design, over a range that brackets the normal operating range on both sides.

source_reference.quote: The margins recorded above are wide on both model viruses, and they establish the small-virus safety of A-Mab drug substance at commercial scale.

weak_claims.rationale: States commercial-scale viral safety from a scale-down estimate, omitting the load limit that the report's own principal finding establishes, the scale-down bound, and the Stage-2 confirmation the lifecycle framework requires. The margins are real; what is unsupported is the leap from them to safety at commercial scale.
weak_claims.correct_version: Capability is estimated from the qualified scale-down model with the parameters within their normal operating ranges and the volumetric load at or below its limit; it is confirmed at commercial scale during Stage 2.

source_reference.quote: Clearance of minute virus of mice (MVM) falls as the volumetric load rises, and that is the only parameter effect the study resolved.
Clearance of xenotropic murine leukaemia virus (XMuLV) and step yield showed no resolved dependence on either parameter over the ranges studied.
Their response-surface models are reported as robustness evidence and are not used predictively.
The clearance credited here is consolidated with the other viral steps in the master report (PCMR-001).
while the antibody monomer, which is smaller than the rating, passes through with the buffer

Small-virus retentive filtration removes virus by size exclusion, low-pH treatment inactivates enveloped virus by acid denaturation (PCR-006), and anion exchange removes virus by charge-based binding (PCR-008).
the purpose of this study was to confirm and bound the platform behaviour for this molecule, not to discover it
The study nonetheless placed pressure in the multivariate design, because an absence of evidence from operation at the set-point is not evidence of robustness across a widened range.
so no effect is aliased with another and both main effects and the interaction are estimated independently
it means the usual caution about a near-saturated screening fit does not apply here
The limitation that does apply is curvature.
The response-surface model described below is the predictive model and is the basis of the design space and of every prediction quoted in this report.
The claim made from the fitted model is then a claim about a region that was actually visited, and no prediction in this report extrapolates beyond a setting at which the step was run.
Three replicates give a poorly determined variance, and the two estimates are not distinguishable on that evidence.
Volumetric load is the only factor the screening study resolved
Clearance depends on how much has been filtered and not on how fast it was filtered, over the ranges studied.
Neither of the other two responses gave a significant term.
The parvovirus model is adequate and is used predictively
They are reported as robustness findings (Appendix C), and no design-space claim rests on either.
Two limitations of the parvovirus model are stated here and carried into every claim made from it.
As filtrate volume accrues, retained virus and the small amount of retained protein build up on and within the membrane, and that accumulated layer changes the local flow path through the membrane.

Pressure sets the flux and hence the time taken to process a given load, but it does not change the size distribution of the challenge and does not change the retention rating of the membrane over the range the step can be operated in.
it means the load limit can be stated as a single number, and not as a limit that varies with the pressure at which the step is run
The design space of the step is the whole characterized rectangle.
Three bounds apply to this design space, and each is a real restriction and not a formality.
Both parameters are proven acceptable across their entire characterization ranges, under both analyses and for both viruses.
The acceptance criterion for a viral clearance response is not a drug-substance specification.
Two bounds close this section.
They are predictions, and confirmation at commercial scale is a Stage 2 activity that the process performance qualification campaign (PPQ) will deliver.
The low-pH hold contributes nothing to parvovirus clearance, because acid treatment does not inactivate a non-enveloped virus, and no credit is taken for it.
Both parameters are classified as well-controlled critical process parameters, and the classification of each rests on a different argument.

Parvovirus clearance is delivered jointly with anion exchange, whose contribution and controls are reported separately (PCR-008), and enveloped-virus clearance is governed by the low-pH hold (PCR-006).
The cumulative claim, the orthogonality argument that permits the contributions to be added, and the comparison of the total against its requirement are consolidated in PCMR-001.
Parvovirus clearance falls with volumetric load, which is the only effect the study resolved
Both parameters are proven acceptable across their full characterization ranges and both are classified as well-controlled critical process parameters.
